parsed.why: Strong visitor-relevant protections, including public-accommodation coverage and a care shield, improve on the national baseline. A documented birth-sex custody placement is a local concern, though dated and relevant chiefly if detained.

Visitor-facing public-accommodation protections, gender-neutral single-occupancy facilities and a care shield make this division markedly more protective. National document and entry-screening restrictions remain substantial exposure.
No mapped facility ban, broad protections and a current care shield improve on the national baseline. Enforcement is not documented, and national document, screening and custody rules still apply.

The minors’ care ban, narrowed adult surgical access, limited statewide recourse and documented local violence worsen the national baseline. The violence counts lack denominators, so they do not establish a targeted campaign.

The division lacks statewide public-accommodation and hate-crime protections; amended certificates retain original sex, and care for minors is barred. No current facility prohibition is documented, but the national restrictions remain.
